name: code
prompt: Write a C++17 function that parses a decimal string into a signed 64-bit integer without exceptions. Reject empty input, whitespace, a sign without digits, non-digits, and overflow. Return std::optional<int64_t>. Include the function only.

name: prose
prompt: Explain in plain language why a cache can improve average latency while making tail latency worse. Use one concrete analogy and keep the explanation under three paragraphs.

name: tool
prompt: Return exactly one compact JSON object for a weather tool call with keys name and arguments. The tool name is get_weather. Arguments must contain city set to Montréal, unit set to celsius, and include_forecast set to true. Do not use Markdown.

name: multilingual
prompt: Répondez en français, puis en japonais. Donnez dans chaque langue deux conseils brefs pour vérifier qu'une sauvegarde peut réellement être restaurée.

name: long-context
prompt: A deployment log records these facts in order: build 814 started at 09:00; unit tests passed at 09:08; the canary reached 10 percent at 09:14; error rate rose from 0.2 percent to 3.7 percent at 09:17; the controller paused rollout at 09:18; an operator changed a database timeout at 09:23; error rate remained above 3 percent; rollback began at 09:27; all instances ran build 813 by 09:34; error rate returned to 0.2 percent at 09:36. Earlier notes say build 812 had a cache-key bug, build 813 fixed it, and build 814 only changed request batching. A separate capacity report says CPU stayed below 55 percent, memory below 68 percent, database connections below 60 percent, and network below 40 percent throughout. The timeout change was reverted after rollback. Summarize the incident as a five-item timeline, identify the most likely change category implicated by the evidence, and explicitly state which four capacity explanations are contradicted by the report. Do not invent a root cause beyond the evidence.
